evidence: products.controller.ts: @Controller('products') class ProductsController exposes only product endpoints (createProduct, getProducts, getProduct, updateProduct, changeStatus, deleteProduct) — one cohesive concern.

products.controller.ts: write handlers delegate entirely to createProductService.execute(dto), updateProductService.execute(id, dto), changeStatusService.execute(id, dto) and deleteProductService.execute(id); there is no validation or invariant logic in the controller.
products.controller.ts: read handlers build new GetProductsQuery(status, limit, offset) and new GetProductQuery(id) and send them through queryBus.execute.
Minor asymmetry: reads go through QueryBus, but writes use services injected directly instead of a CommandBus. It is consistent within each side, so it is not treated as a bypass.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit has one file, src/products/presentation/products.controller.ts, and it is a single HTTP adapter for the products resource. Every handler only maps HTTP input to a call on an application use-case service or a CQRS query, then shapes the response. The controller holds no business rules or invariants, so nothing is duplicated, and it never touches repositories or domain entities directly, so no abstraction is bypassed. One inconsistency is noted but not judged a failure: reads go through QueryBus with query objects, while writes call injected use-case services directly instead of a CommandBus. This looks like a deliberate split between commands and queries rather than a bypass of one of the module's own abstractions, but it does mean there are two ways of sending requests to the application layer.
